title_en: Behavior-Chain Detection for Remote Access Tools (Tool-Agnostic)

analytics.description_en: Chain of remote access tool behavior: (1) initial execution of remote-control/assist agent or GUI under user context; (2) persistence via service or autorun; (3) long-lived outbound connection/tunnel to external infrastructure; (4) interactive control signals such as shell or file-manager child processes spawned by the RAT parent.

mutable_elements.description_en: Correlation period binding start→persistence→egress→child (default 15m, adjust per environment).
Differentiate help-desk/jump hosts and admin accounts from standard endpoints.
Known-good remote support tools; suppress expected events while still correlating anomalous sequences.
Alert when services/agents execute from user-writable or temp paths.
Vendors’ support clouds/CDNs to reduce false positives on egress detection.
Define which child shells from GUI parents are acceptable versus suspicious.
Thresholds for session duration, connection counts, and bytes_out/bytes_in ratio.

analytics.description_en: Sequence of RAT agent execution, systemd persistence, and long-lived external egress; optional interactive shells spawned from the agent.

log_sources.channel: execve: Agent/headless flags (listen/connect/reverse/tunnel) or remote-control binaries spawning shells

mutable_elements.description_en: Bind exec→service→egress events; extend for staged deployments.

Define shells/interpreters considered anomalous when spawned by GUI/agent parents.
Flow heuristics for long-lived, client-heavy connections post-install.

analytics.description_en: Electron/GUI or headless RAT execution followed by LaunchAgent/Daemon persistence and persistent external connections; interactive children (osascript/sh/curl) spawned by parent.

log_sources.channel: Process exec of remote-control apps or binaries with headless/connect flags
CREATE/MODIFY: Creation of LaunchAgents/Daemons plists in user/system locations
CONNECT: Long-lived connections from remote-control parents to external IPs/domains

mutable_elements.description_en: Legitimate remote-support apps under /Applications.
Known-good LaunchAgents/Daemons identifiers.
Window for correlating exec→launchd→egress events.
Duration/volume thresholds for persistent sessions.

delete: Modification of systemd unit files or config for security agents

mutable_elements.description_en: List of endpoint protection service names (varies across deployments).
Accounts permitted to legitimately stop or reconfigure services.

mutable_elements.description_en: Authorized management sources.

title_en: Behavior‑chain detection for T1134.003 Make and Impersonate Token (Windows)

analytics.description_en: A process creates a brand‑new logon session/token (LogonUser /LsaLogonUser) and then assigns/impersonates it (SetThreadToken/ImpersonateLoggedOnUser) to run actions under that freshly created security context. Chain: (1) suspicious command or script block (e.g., runas /netonly, PowerShell P/Invoke of LogonUser) → (2) ETW/API evidence of LogonUser /SetThreadToken → (3) Security 4624 New Logon (often LogonType=9 NewCredentials or 2/3 from a non‑interactive parent) with no interactive desktop → (4) sysmon 1 process(es) executing with the new LogonId/SID different from the parent process → (5) optional privileged ops/lateral movement.

mutable_elements.description_en: Correlation window between LogonUser*/SetThreadToken and the first spawned process (default 5–10 minutes).
Which 4624 LogonTypes to treat as high risk (e.g., 9 NewCredentials, 3 Network when sourced locally).
Processes/accounts legitimately creating tokens (e.g., winlogon.exe, lsass.exe, IIS worker, trusted service accounts).
Whether to alert on any SID/LogonId mismatch between parent/child not in allow-list.
Minimum integrity level jump (e.g., Medium→High/System) to raise severity.

analytics.description_en: Creation of outbound connections on alternate ports or using covert transport (e.g., ICMP, DNS) from non-network-intensive processes, following known disruption or blocked traffic.

mutable_elements.description_en: Can filter for rare fallback channel types (e.g., ICMP, DNS over HTTP).
Tuning by user (e.g., root vs. service account) helps suppress noise.

analytics.description_en: Outbound fallback traffic from low-profile or background launch agents using unusual protocols or destinations after primary channel inactivity.

mutable_elements.description_en: Used to suppress known legitimate agents.
Can help isolate covert or encrypted fallback traffic.

analytics.description_en: Outbound traffic from host management services or guest-to-host interactions over unusual interfaces (e.g., backdoor API endpoints or external VPN tunnels).

mutable_elements.description_en: May vary based on ESXi build and should be filtered to suppress known interfaces.
Environment-specific ranges to ignore (e.g., DR tunnels or out-of-band mgmt).

title_en: Detection Strategy for Compile After Delivery - Source Code to Executable Transformation

Tune the correlation window between compilation and subsequent execution or C2

Monitor for output files in user-writable paths (e.g., `~/Library/Caches`, `~/Downloads`)

Enable or disable detection of Alternate Data Streams depending on business use.

Creation of hidden files (.*) in sensitive directories (/etc, /var, /usr/bin)

mutable_elements.description_en: Restrict hidden file detection to privileged system directories.
Tune for specific chattr flags (+i immutable, +a append-only) most abused for persistence.

Creation of LaunchAgents/LaunchDaemons in hidden or non-standard directories

Datastore file hidden or renamed unexpectedly

Indicators of manual encryption operations (e.g., script strings invoking AES).

Expected egress destinations and volume for core services.
